title: Speaking & Writing
subject: Bahasa Inggris
prerequisites: Peserta didik telah mempelajari kosakata tambahan dan memahami teks tentang mendeskripsikan dan membandingkan dua orang.
resources: Sumber Belajar:  Rise Up! Teens! Student Book 1, page 30-31
Laptop/ komputer, pengeras suara, projector, PPT
learningModel: Discovery Learning, Task-Based Learning, Tatap Muka.
approach: Peserta didik diajak untuk fokus dan saksama saat menyimak audio, mengamati detail gambar/komik, dan memperhatikan struktur bahasa yang digunakan.
Peserta didik menghubungkan materi pembelajaran dengan pengalaman dan kehidupan nyata mereka, sehingga pembelajaran terasa relevan dan bermanfaat.
Pembelajaran dikemas dalam aktivitas yang menyenangkan seperti permainan tebak hobi, kerja kelompok, penggunaan komik strip, dan survei interaktif.
objectives: Learners will be able to speak and write about describing and comparing three or more people or places.
Learners will understand that all of us have strengths and weaknesses.

details: Greet the students and ask about their feelings. For example: “How are you feeling today?” or “How would you describe your mood in one word?”
The teacher introduces himself/herself in front of the class.
Get to know the students by using the letter game.
The teacher writes down his/her name on the board (e.g. Susan)
Ask the student if their name starts with the shown letter (e.g. starts with S) and then they must stand up and introduce themselves. Continue with other letters.
Other alternatives to get to know the students: hot potato and throw the ball.
Ask students to look at Student Book page 30.
First, the teacher reads the questions in the speech bubble at the top of the page aloud for the students to hear.
Next, the teacher asks everyone to read the questions aloud as a class.
Then, ask students to ask and answer the questions, in pairs.
Model to the students how the questions can be changed by changing some of the key vocabulary in the questions.

Now, put them in different pairs and ask them to substitute some of the key vocabulary in the questions so they can practice asking about different things. This can be repeated several times by putting students into different pairs.
To finish the speaking activity, elicit responses from some students by asking the questions in the speech bubbles with the original vocabulary, and also with some substituted vocabulary.
Check the Teacher’s Guide to see further explanation about the Language Box (meaning, form, use, common mistakes). This can be used to help answer students' questions.
Ask students to look at Student Book page 30 and complete questions 1-4 by writing an -est word on each line. Choose four of the words given in the gray box under the instructions.

Then they have to ask their completed questions to other classmates. They should ask eight students in total. This can be done by moving around the classroom and choosing a new partner after each question.
They should write their partners' names and answers in their books.
Read the example question and answers aloud together as a class. Students are instructed to follow the structures shown in the Q&A models and Language Box.
Once they understand the task, they can begin and  move around the room until all 4 boxes are filled in.
Then, elicit example questions and answers from the class. Answers will vary a lot because of the questions each student creates, and the individual answers that their partners will give.
This is an additional activity for further practice if there is time.
Tell students they will ask and answer questions about a family.
There is information about two families below. Choose the most suitable family for your classroom. (look at the Teacher’s Guide)
• Write these questions on the board:
- Who is the ___________ in the family?

Ask students to write four questions in their notebooks about the family using the question model above and to fill the gap using -est words. Guide students to look at page 30 to see the words they can choose from.
Put students in pairs and they will ask and answer the questions they have written in their notebooks. Tell them to write their partner’s answers in their notebooks.
Ask around five pairs of students to read one of their questions and answers aloud to the class.
Give corrective feedback for common mistakes. Look at the Language Tips for Teachers, Section 4. Common Mistakes, and write some of these on the board for students to look at and correct.
Direct the students to look at the pictures on page 31 and ask them ‘“What can you see on the page?” to elicit some answers.
Next, tell students to read the text about the Teen Value. They can read it silently, or put them in pairs to share reading the text aloud together, sentence by sentence.
Elicit from students, “What is the key focus of this Teen Corner page?”, and “Why do you think this skill (or value) is important?”
Ask students to look at activity A and give them around 3-4 minutes to discuss how the students in the picture are making a good impression.

Before completing activity A, read the text together. Teachers can divide the class into 3-4 groups or each row (if the desks are lined up in a grid). Each group or row can read 2 sentences, do it alternately from the first to the last sentence.
Read through the strengths and weaknesses to make sure students understand the vocabulary and ask them to write down their strengths and weaknesses.

Remind them that everyone has strengths and weaknesses, and that if we can identify our strengths and weaknesses, we can think about how to work on overcoming our weaknesses possibly by using our strengths.
Tell students to find a partner and tell them about their strengths and weaknesses.
Because this might be a sensitive topic to share, make sure students choose their own groups to work with.
Give around 5 minutes for this activity.
Ask students to look at Activity C.
The idea is to say nice things about other classmates in order to build good relationships amongst students.

If individual students are too nervous to come to the class and say three nice things about the student whose name they get on a piece of paper, ask two students to come and work together to say the three nice things.
If there is not enough time to do this for every student, try to do at least 8-10 names.
Read the text in the 'Being Self-Aware' aloud to the class.
Ask students why it is important to be self-aware, as a way to summarize the aim of the lesson.
Ask 4-5 students to share their answers with the class.

Wrap up the class by highlighting that everyone has strengths and weaknesses. Being able to identify this is essential to help them overcome their weaknesses, and also to connect better with other people.
Conclude the lesson, give feedback, and appreciation toward the student(s) / the whole class. Dismiss the class.

assessment: Asesmen formatif: unjuk kerja speaking berpasangan (kelancaran, ketepatan, keberanian).
Produk tulisan sederhana sesuai model di Student Book (struktur & kosakata unit).
Umpan balik teman sebaya dan guru terhadap hasil speaking/writing.
reflectionStudent: Apa hal baru yang kamu pelajari hari ini?
Bagian mana yang paling mudah dan paling sulit bagimu? Mengapa?
Kalimat bahasa Inggris apa yang sudah bisa kamu ucapkan dengan percaya diri?
Apa yang akan kamu lakukan untuk berlatih di rumah?
reflectionTeacher: Apakah tujuan pembelajaran tercapai? Bukti apa yang menunjukkannya?
Kegiatan mana yang paling efektif dan mana yang perlu diperbaiki?
Berapa persen instruksi kelas yang disampaikan dalam bahasa Inggris?
Peserta didik mana yang memerlukan pendampingan atau pengayaan?
